name: Miller's flask and the honest gap
scope: The origin-of-life experiment that worked -- and the distance it did not cover. T1: in December 1952 a 22-year-old University of Chicago graduate student, Stanley Miller, sealed methane, ammonia, hydrogen and boiling water into a loop of glass and ran an electric spark through it for one week to imitate lightning over a young ocean -- and the water turned a murky pink-brown with amino acids, the building blocks of protein (the hook: a spark, a week, and life's bricks appear from nothing living). T2: his Nobel-winning supervisor Harold Urey had wanted him to do a safer project on thallium in meteorites; Miller talked him into the origin-of-life run, and the 1953 Science paper 'A Production of Amino Acids Under Possible Primitive Earth Conditions' carried Miller's name first, not the famous professor's. T3: the mechanism -- the spark cracks methane and ammonia into hydrogen cyanide and formaldehyde, which recombine by Strecker synthesis into glycine and alpha-alanine; ordinary chemistry, no vital spark required. T4: the honest accounting nobody puts on the poster -- only about 2 percent of the carbon ended up as amino acids, no sugars and no nucleotides appeared at all, and 80-90 percent of the product was a brown tar that coated the glass. T4b: the assumption underneath has weakened -- geochemists now read Archean rocks as evidence that early air was mostly carbon dioxide and nitrogen, not the strongly reducing methane-ammonia mix Miller used, and neutral-gas reruns give amino-acid yields orders of magnitude lower. T5: in 2008, a year after Miller died, Jeffrey Bada and Adam Johnson reopened his labelled vials from a 1952-54 volcanic steam-and-spark variant and found 22 amino acids and 5 amines with modern instruments -- more than Miller could detect in 1953, from samples that had sat in a box for fifty years. T5b: the leading candidate for the first replicator is RNA, because Walter Gilbert (1986) named the 'RNA world' after ribozymes showed a single molecule can both carry information and catalyse reactions -- one molecule doing both of DNA's and protein's jobs. T5c: the gap the bank refuses to paper over -- amino acids are bricks, and no one has yet built a self-copying, self-enclosing cell from them; homochirality (life uses only left-handed amino acids, while Miller's flask made both hands equally) and the origin of the first replicator are open. Rival sites -- Darwin's 1871 'warm little pond' letter to Joseph Hooker versus alkaline hydrothermal vents -- are competing hypotheses, not a settled answer.
source: Grokipedia 'Miller-Urey experiment' (read in full via browser -- apparatus assembled 13 Dec 1952, CH4 200 mmHg / NH3 200 mmHg / H2 100 mmHg, tungsten electrodes ~1 cm apart, one week, glycine + alpha-alanine + beta-alanine confirmed, ~2% carbon into amino acids, 80-90% tar, reducing-atmosphere critique from Archean komatiite/basalt redox and the QFM buffer, no nucleotides or sugars); Wikipedia 'Abiogenesis' (Gilbert coined 'RNA world' 1986; Rich 1962; Darwin's 1871 letter to Hooker quoted; Szostak/Chen protocells; 3.48 Ga Dresser Formation stromatolites, 3.7 Ga Isua/Akilia biogenic carbon, 4.1 Ga Jack Hills zircon graphite; 'derivation of LUCA from simple components is far from understood'); Wikipedia 'Stanley Miller' (2008 Bada + Adam Johnson reanalysis of archived vials from the 1952-54 apparatuses, 22 amino acids + 5 amines by HPLC and LC-TOF-MS; Science paper 15 May 1953; Miller died May 2007). BUILD NOTE: Grokipedia not yet read for the RNA-world / homochirality / hydrothermal-vent rungs -- run Grokipedia-first on those before authoring.
framing_note: Flagship MYSTERY ladder, told as a DISCOVERY that succeeded and then honestly stopped. T1 keys the ACT and the visible result (spark, one week, murky flask of amino acids), never a definition of abiogenesis. ACCURACY RAIL (the one that matters): the experiment ran from December 1952 and published in 1953, and it made AMINO ACIDS -- it never made a cell, a protein, DNA or life; any rung that lets a kid think Miller 'created life in a jar' is a failure. Second rail: the reducing-atmosphere assumption is now doubted, so state it as an assumption that was tested and weakened, not as a debunking of the chemistry. Dinner-test payoff: T1. T5 must say 'no one yet knows' proudly -- the first replicator and homochirality are open, and NO distractor may secretly be the true answer. Distractor mine: the real graveyard and the real live rivals -- spontaneous generation (which Pasteur killed), Oparin-Haldane primordial soup, panspermia (Arrhenius; Crick's directed panspermia), Wachtershauser's iron-sulfur world, Cairns-Smith's clay templates, alkaline hydrothermal vents -- every one held by serious scientists, which is the point. Anti-restatement: describe the FLASK and what came out of it, never announce 'amino acids can form abiotically' before asking what Miller found. LANE: the philosophy bank owns design arguments and 'why is there life at all'; science keys the flask, the measured yield, and the named gap.
history_overlap: philosophy bank -- origin-of-life and design/first-cause arguments are philosophy's ground; science must key the apparatus, the 2% yield, the tar and the named unsolved problems, never the metaphysics. Animal bank -- common descent and LUCA framing; keep science on pre-life chemistry.

name: The hard problem: why anything feels like anything
scope: The scientific state of play on consciousness -- experiments and scoreboards, not seminar arguments. T1: every day, in ordinary operating theatres, anaesthetists switch a person's inner experience off and then back on -- and nobody can say what physical thing is being switched (the hook: a routine procedure nobody can explain). T2: David Chalmers named the split at the 1994 Tucson 'Toward a Science of Consciousness' conference and published it in 1995 -- the EASY problems (how the eye routes signals, how attention selects, how a brain reports on its own states) are hard engineering but ordinary science; the HARD problem is why performing any of those functions is accompanied by experience at all. T3: Thomas Nagel's 1974 essay set the shape with a bat -- you can learn every detail of how echolocation works and still not know what echolocating is LIKE from the inside; that residue is what the science has to explain. T4: two rival theories make DIFFERENT, testable brain predictions -- Giulio Tononi's Integrated Information Theory says consciousness tracks how much a system's information is integrated and predicts the back of the cortex carries it, while Global Neuronal Workspace (Stanislas Dehaene, Bernard Baars) says consciousness is information broadcast brain-wide and predicts the prefrontal cortex lights up. T5: instead of arguing in journals, the COGITATE adversarial collaboration made both camps PRE-REGISTER what their theory predicted before the scanning started; the peer-reviewed result appeared in Nature on 30 April 2025 and vindicated neither cleanly -- two of three IIT predictions passed the threshold, none of GNWT's did, and both theories were forced to update. T5b: the scoreboard nobody spins -- Christof Koch bet David Chalmers a case of fine wine that the neural basis of consciousness would be pinned down within 25 years; when the 25 years ran out in 2023, Koch paid up. T5c: in September 2023, 124 researchers signed an open letter arguing IIT should be labelled pseudoscience until it makes sharper testable predictions -- a live, public fight about where the border of science runs, with defenders answering in print.
source: Wikipedia 'Hard problem of consciousness' (Chalmers formulated it at the 1994 Tucson conference and published 'Facing up to the problem of consciousness' in 1995 in the Journal of Consciousness Studies, expanded in The Conscious Mind 1996; the easy/hard split and the 'why is the performance of these functions accompanied by experience?' formulation; Nagel 1974 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?'; Levine 1983 explanatory gap); Wikipedia 'Integrated information theory' (COGITATE adversarial collaboration funded by the Templeton Foundation, initial results June 2023, final peer-reviewed results in Nature 30 April 2025 -- two of three IIT predictions passed the pre-registration threshold, none of GNWT's did; September 2023 open letter signed by 124 scholars calling IIT pseudoscience, defenders responded, a later survey found only 8% fully agreed); Wikipedia 'Christof Koch' (25-year bet with Chalmers, stake a case of fine wine, Koch lost in 2023 and delivered the wine; the article does not state the 1998 start date explicitly). BUILD NOTE: Grokipedia not yet read for this topic -- run Grokipedia-first on 'Hard problem of consciousness' and 'Integrated information theory'; verify the bet's 1998 start date and the June 2023 ASSC venue from a primary or news source before any rung names them.
framing_note: MYSTERY plus METHOD. This is the tightest LANE BORDER in the sub-strand: the philosophy bank owns qualia, zombies, Mary's Room and the mind-body problem -- the SCIENCE bank keys the experiments and the public scoreboard (pre-registration, adversarial collaboration, the lost bet, the pseudoscience letter, anaesthesia). If a candidate rung could sit unchanged in a philosophy seminar, it belongs to philosophy; cut it. T1 must be concrete and picturable (the anaesthetic switch), never 'what is consciousness?'. ACCURACY RAIL: Chalmers NAMED the hard problem in a 1994 Tucson talk and PUBLISHED it in 1995 -- do not merge those into one event; and never write a rung implying science has explained consciousness or is close. Dinner-test payoff: T5b (a neuroscientist bet a philosopher a case of wine that the brain would give up the answer in 25 years, and lost). MYSTERY DISCIPLINE: no distractor may secretly be the true explanation -- on this topic there is no accepted answer, so mechanism rungs must ask what a NAMED theory PREDICTED or what a NAMED experiment FOUND. Distractor mine: real rival theories real scientists hold -- Global Neuronal Workspace, Higher-Order Thought, predictive processing, Penrose-Hameroff orchestrated objective reduction -- plus the respectable-but-abandoned (Descartes' pineal gland; behaviourism's ruling that inner experience is not a scientific object). Teach 'pre-registration' and 'adversarial collaboration' before testing them.
history_overlap: philosophy bank -- Nagel's bat, qualia, the explanatory gap, philosophical zombies and the mind-body problem are philosophy-bank property; the science rungs must anchor on COGITATE, the Koch-Chalmers bet, anaesthesia and the IIT-vs-GNWT brain predictions instead.

name: Why we sleep -- a third of your life, unexplained
scope: The most-used mystery in biology. T1: you spend roughly a third of your life unconscious, motionless and defenceless -- an arrangement that ought to be an evolutionary disaster -- and every animal with a brain does it anyway (the hook: the cost is obvious and the payoff is not). T2: Allan Rechtschaffen's University of Chicago rats, kept awake on a disk over water, died after about two to three weeks without sleep, losing weight while eating more and failing to hold their body temperature -- proof that sleep is not optional -- and yet the autopsies never yielded a clean cause of death. T3: the memory theory -- sleep replays the day's activity and stabilises what was learned, which is why a night's sleep beats an all-nighter on a memory test. T4: the cleaning theory, and the one you will hear on television: Maiken Nedergaard's lab reported in Science in 2013 that the fluid spaces between brain cells widen during sleep and flush metabolic waste, including beta-amyloid -- the 'glymphatic' idea. T5: in June 2024 Nick Franks and Bill Wisden's Imperial College team published the opposite result in Nature Neuroscience -- tracer cleared from mouse brains MORE SLOWLY during sleep and anaesthesia -- so the brain-washing story is contested, not settled. T5b: a third live theory, Giulio Tononi and Chiara Cirelli's synaptic homeostasis hypothesis: during waking, synapses strengthen until the brain saturates, and sleep prunes them back down so tomorrow can be learned. T5c: even celebrated popular science gets audited -- in December 2019 an independent writer, Alexey Guzey, published a line-by-line critique of Matthew Walker's bestselling 'Why We Sleep', and the statistician Andrew Gelman flagged a bar removed from one of its graphs; scrutiny does not stop at the bestseller list. T5d: Rechtschaffen's own verdict on the whole field -- if sleep does not serve a vital function, it is the biggest mistake the evolutionary process ever made.
source: Wikipedia 'Sleep' (anabolic/restorative framing; the sleeping brain removes metabolic end products faster than the waking brain; memory consolidation of declarative and procedural memory); Wikipedia 'Allan Rechtschaffen' (experiments in rats demonstrating the lethal consequences of long-term -- two weeks or more -- sleep deprivation and REM deprivation); PubMed record for Miao A, Luo T, Hsieh B, Edge CJ, Gridley M, Wong RTC, Constandinou TG, Wisden W, Franks NP, 'Brain clearance is reduced during sleep and anesthesia', Nature Neuroscience 27(6):1046-1050, June 2024 (main finding: clearance markedly REDUCED during sleep and anaesthesia, contradicting the prevailing hypothesis); Wikipedia 'Glymphatic system' (2013 finding that slow-wave sleep expands the extracellular space and increases interstitial solute clearance); Wikipedia 'Why We Sleep' (Guzey's December 2019 critique essay; Andrew Gelman on the removed graph bar as a possible 'smoking gun'; Walker's 2019 blog responses). BUILD NOTE: Grokipedia not yet read for this topic -- run Grokipedia-first on 'Sleep', 'Glymphatic system' and 'Sleep deprivation'; verify the Rechtschaffen 'biggest mistake evolution ever made' wording against Rechtschaffen 1971 / his 1998 'Current perspectives on the function of sleep' before quoting it, and describe the idea without quotation marks if it cannot be sourced.
framing_note: Flagship MYSTERY ladder with a built-in REVERSAL. T1 keys the everyday scandal a ten-year-old can feel (a third of your life, defenceless, for reasons unknown). ACCURACY RAIL (load-bearing): the glymphatic sleep-cleaning story is CONTESTED as of 2024 -- the 2013 Nedergaard/Xie result and the 2024 Miao/Franks/Wisden contradiction must both appear, and no rung may assert 'sleep washes the brain' as settled fact. Second rail: Rechtschaffen's rats prove sleep is NECESSARY, not what it is FOR -- do not let the experiment be written up as if it answered the question. Dinner-test payoff: T5 (the famous brain-washing result was contradicted by the opposite finding in 2024). MYSTERY DISCIPLINE: every candidate function is live, so no distractor may secretly be the truth -- mechanism rungs must ask which theory a NAMED researcher proposed or what a NAMED experiment measured, never 'what is sleep for?'. Distractor mine: the rival theories themselves, all held by real researchers -- energy conservation, predator-avoidance/enforced inactivity, immune function, thermoregulation, synaptic homeostasis, glymphatic clearance, memory consolidation. LANE: dolphins and birds sleeping one hemisphere at a time is CREATURE behaviour and belongs to the animal bank; keep science on human physiology and the contested mechanism. Handle T5c as record, not sermon -- an outsider audited a famous expert and a statistician backed him; present it and move on.
history_overlap: animal bank -- unihemispheric sleep in dolphins and birds, per-species sleep durations, hibernation and migratory sleeplessness belong there; science keeps the human physiology, the Rechtschaffen rats as an EXPERIMENT, and the contested mechanism.

name: In search of the engram
scope: A century-long hunt for the place a memory physically lives. T1: Karl Lashley spent about thirty years training rats to run mazes and then cutting pieces out of their cortex to find where the maze memory was kept -- and never found it; cutting MORE tissue made performance worse, but WHERE he cut barely mattered. T2: the word he was hunting -- 'engram', the physical trace a memory leaves behind -- had been coined in 1904 by Richard Semon, decades before any instrument existed that could look for one. T3: Lashley's 1950 summary of his own failure, half joke and half despair: the evidence made him wonder whether learning was possible at all; his principles of mass action and equipotentiality said cortical memory is spread out, not filed in one drawer. T4: in 2012 Susumu Tonegawa's MIT lab (Liu and colleagues, Nature) tagged the exact dentate gyrus neurons that fired while a mouse learned to fear one box, then switched only those cells back on with a pulse of light while the mouse sat in a different, completely safe box -- and the mouse froze. The engram was shown to be a specific, findable set of cells. T5: the following year the same lab went further and implanted a FALSE fear memory -- a mouse afraid of a place where nothing bad had ever happened to it. T5b: the part still unsolved -- the proteins inside a synapse are replaced within days to weeks, yet a memory can last sixty years; what physically persists (synaptic strength, whole-cell ensembles, molecules inside the nucleus, the scaffolding between cells) is still argued, so the engram has been located without being explained.
source: Wikipedia 'Engram (neuropsychology)' (Semon introduced 'engram' in 1904 as 'the physical substrate of memory in the organism'; Lashley's 1920s maze-and-lesion rat studies showing lesion SIZE mattered and LOCATION did not; Liu et al. 2012 MIT optogenetic reactivation of hippocampal engram cells described as 'highly specific physical activation of a specific small subpopulation of brain cells'; artificial implantation of false memories in animal models; unresolved questions listed explicitly -- synaptic versus non-synaptic encoding, the molecular substrate that survives continuous protein turnover, and how engrams achieve long-term physical stability). BUILD NOTE: Grokipedia not yet read for this topic -- run Grokipedia-first on 'Engram' and 'Karl Lashley'; verify the exact wording and 1950 venue of Lashley's 'In Search of the Engram' conclusion, and verify the James McConnell planarian memory-transfer episode independently before using it as a distractor or a rung.
framing_note: MYSTERY told through a DISCOVERY that half-succeeded. T1 keys the vivid failure (thirty years of cutting, and the memory was never in the piece he removed) -- never 'what is an engram?'. ACCURACY RAIL: Lashley did not show memory has no physical location; he showed cortical maze memory is DISTRIBUTED, and his result is about lesion size versus lesion site. Second rail: Tonegawa's lab REACTIVATED an existing memory in 2012 and IMPLANTED a false one in 2013 -- two experiments, two rungs, never merged. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (a flash of light in a safe box makes a mouse freeze with fear it learned somewhere else). MYSTERY DISCIPLINE: T5b must say plainly that how a memory outlasts its own molecules is unresolved, and no distractor may secretly be the answer. Distractor mine: real memory substrates real scientists proposed -- Donald Hebb's cell assemblies, Eric Kandel's synaptic strengthening in Aplysia, protein synthesis and CREB, the hippocampus-as-index idea -- plus the perfect respectable-but-wrong entry, James McConnell's 1960s planarian experiments claiming memory could be transferred by feeding trained flatworms to untrained ones, taken seriously at the time and now rejected. Teach 'optogenetics' in plain words (a light-operated switch installed in chosen cells) before any rung tests it.

name: Turbulence: the swirl in your coffee no equation tames
scope: The unsolved problem sitting in a coffee cup. T1: stir milk into coffee once and watch -- the ribbon breaks into curls, and inside those curls are smaller curls, and no physicist alive can write an equation that predicts where any individual curl will go (the hook: the famous unsolved problem is on your kitchen table and you can run it right now). T2: Osborne Reynolds, Manchester 1883, ran a thin thread of dye down the centre of water flowing through a glass pipe: at low speed the dye held a clean straight line all the way down the tube; past a threshold speed it burst apart and filled the whole cross-section -- the first clean laboratory picture of the transition to turbulence, published as 'An experimental investigation of the circumstances which determine whether the motion of water shall be direct or sinuous'. T3: Lewis Fry Richardson caught the structure in a rhyme in 'Weather Prediction by Numerical Process' (1922, p. 66): 'Big whirls have little whirls that feed on their velocity, and little whirls have lesser whirls and so on to viscosity' -- energy cascading down from large eddies to smaller ones until friction finally eats it. T4: Andrey Kolmogorov's 1941 theory gave the cascade a number -- the minus-five-thirds energy spectrum -- and measurements confirm it; but real flows deviate from Kolmogorov's statistics in bursts (intermittency), so the best statistical theory of turbulence is known to be incomplete. T5: the equations have existed since the 1840s -- the Navier-Stokes equations -- and nobody has proved that their solutions in three dimensions always stay smooth rather than blowing up; the Clay Mathematics Institute lists Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems, with a million dollars unclaimed. T5b: what the gap costs -- weather forecasts decay after about a week, aircraft still need wind tunnels and supercomputers instead of a formula, and 'we have the equation' turns out not to mean 'we can solve it'.
source: Wikipedia 'Turbulence' (turbulence listed among the unsolved problems in physics; Kolmogorov 1941 energy cascade and its breakdown at higher scales; the Reynolds number predicting onset; the minus-5/3 spectrum empirically validated; NOTE: the article attributes 'the most important unsolved problem in classical physics' to Feynman WITHOUT giving a primary source); Wikipedia 'Osborne Reynolds' (the 1883 glass-pipe dye-filament experiment -- dyed layer distinct at low velocity, then breaking up and diffusing across the cross-section; Reynolds number as the ratio of inertial to viscous forces; the full 1883 Proceedings of the Royal Society title); Wikipedia 'Lewis Fry Richardson' (the whirls rhyme quoted with its source, 'Weather Prediction by Numerical Process', 1922, p. 66; the 1922 forecast-factory; the coastline/Richardson effect later cited by Mandelbrot 1967); Wikipedia 'List of unsolved problems in physics' (turbulence entry phrased as whether a theoretical model can describe the statistics of turbulent flow -- and carrying NO Feynman attribution). BUILD NOTE: Grokipedia not yet read -- run Grokipedia-first on 'Turbulence' and 'Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness'; feynmanlectures.caltech.edu returned HTTP 403 and Wikiquote's Feynman page carries no turbulence quote, so the famous line could NOT be traced to a primary text.
framing_note: CONCEPT/THEME ladder -- native T4/T5 ceiling, and the analytic backbone of this sub-strand. ACCURACY RAIL (the one that matters most here): the punchy line calling turbulence 'the most important unsolved problem of classical physics' is WIDELY attributed to Feynman but I could not trace it to any primary Feynman text -- Wikiquote does not carry it and the Feynman Lectures site was unreachable. Do NOT set it in quotation marks as a Feynman quote. If a quote rung is wanted, use Richardson's whirls rhyme, which is documented to Weather Prediction by Numerical Process (1922, p. 66). Second rail: Navier-Stokes is not 'unsolvable' -- engineers simulate turbulent flow successfully every day; the open question is the existence and smoothness of solutions in three dimensions. State the gap precisely. Dinner-test payoff: T1, and frame it as an INVITATION -- stir a cup and watch an unsolved problem happen. Distractor mine: adjacent fluid ideas that are real but answer a DIFFERENT question (Prandtl's boundary layer, the von Karman vortex street, Bernoulli's principle, the Reynolds number as an onset criterion) plus the genuine graveyard (the luminiferous ether, caloric, and the equal-transit-time wing myth, which is worth its own corrected-misconception rung). Teach 'viscosity' and 'eddy' before testing them.
history_overlap: geography bank -- jet stream, ocean gyres, hurricane structure and named storm systems are PLACE-anchored earth processes there; science must key Reynolds' pipe, Richardson's cascade, Kolmogorov's spectrum and the Millennium Prize gap, not a tour of weather systems.

name: The superconductor nobody can explain
scope: A forty-year-old mechanism gap, and the discipline that keeps room-temperature claims honest. T1: cool the right ceramic below its critical temperature and a magnet parked above it stops falling and simply hovers there, held up and locked in place -- a demonstration a classroom can watch, powered by a material that carries current with exactly zero resistance. T2: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes found it first in Leiden in 1911: mercury cooled to about 4.2 K did not merely lose most of its resistance, it dropped to ZERO, abruptly -- a cliff rather than a slope. T3: the mechanism for ordinary superconductors was solved in 1957 by Bardeen, Cooper and Schrieffer -- vibrations of the crystal lattice glue electrons into Cooper pairs -- and that theory implied a ceiling near 30 K, which is why the field stalled at 23 K for over a decade. T4: in 1986 Georg Bednorz and Alex Muller at IBM Zurich found superconductivity at 35 K in a lanthanum-barium-copper-oxide CERAMIC -- a brittle oxide of exactly the sort metal physicists had written off -- and were given the Nobel Prize the very next year, 1987. T4b: within months Ching-Wu Chu and Maw-Kuen Wu pushed yttrium-barium-copper-oxide to 93 K, above liquid nitrogen's boiling point of 77 K, which changed the coolant from scarce liquid helium to a cheap liquid you can pour out of a flask. T5: forty years on, NOBODY has an accepted explanation of why the cuprates superconduct -- the tiny or inverted isotope effect says lattice vibrations alone cannot be the glue, and the pseudogap and stripe phases are still argued over; the mechanism is openly unsolved while the material sits inside working magnets. T5b: the extraordinary-claims drill, case one -- in July 2023 Sukbae Lee and Ji-Hoon Kim posted preprints claiming LK-99, a copper-doped lead apatite, superconducted at room temperature and ordinary pressure; a video of a fragment half-lifting off a magnet went viral; within about three weeks laboratories worldwide, including a Max Planck group growing pure single crystals, showed the resistance drop came from a copper sulfide impurity and the partial lift from ferromagnetic contamination. Science did not debate the claim -- it MADE the stuff. T5c: case two -- Ranga Dias published room-temperature superconductivity in Nature in October 2020 (about 15 C, at 267 GPa) and again in March 2023 (about 20.5 C, near 1 GPa); the first was retracted in September 2022, the second on 7 November 2023 at the request of eight of his own co-authors, and a 2024 University of Rochester investigation concluded he had falsified and fabricated data. Jorge Hirsch, the physicist who questioned the data first and was brushed off, was right.
source: Grokipedia 'High-temperature superconductivity' (read via browser -- Onnes 1911 mercury at ~4.2 K; Meissner and Ochsenfeld 1933; isotope effect Maxwell / Reynolds 1950; BCS 1957 and the ~30 K McMillan ceiling; Nb3Ge 23 K record by 1973; Bednorz and Muller 1986 La-Ba-Cu-O at 35 K onset in Zeitschrift fur Physik B, Nobel 1987; Chu and Wu 1987 YBa2Cu3O7 at 93 K, above liquid nitrogen's 77 K; HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8 to ~133-135 K at ambient pressure; iron-based superconductors 2008 up to 56 K; H3S ~203 K at 155 GPa and LaH10 ~250 K at 170 GPa; negligible or inverse isotope effect, pseudogap, stripe phases; the pairing mechanism explicitly unresolved; coherence lengths 1-2 nm; ceramic brittleness); Wikipedia 'LK-99' (Sukbae Lee and Ji-Hoon Kim, Quantum Energy Research Centre, July 2023 arXiv preprints claiming up to 400 K at ambient pressure; viral partial-levitation video on Bilibili in early August 2023; Kapil Kumar's 31 July structural confirmation without strong diamagnetism; Max Planck single crystals 11 August; Cu2S impurity explaining the resistivity drop and ferromagnetic impurities the partial levitation; Nature declaring the claim dead 16 August 2023); Wikipedia 'Ranga P. Dias' (October 2020 Nature carbonaceous sulfur hydride at ~15 C / 267 GPa, retracted September 2022; March 2023 nitrogen-doped lutetium hydride at ~20.5 C near 1 GPa, retracted 7 November 2023 at the request of eight co-authors over Dias's objection; March 2024 University of Rochester investigation finding research misconduct including falsification and fabrication; no longer employed there as of 19 November 2024; Jorge Hirsch first to question the data, Marvin Cohen raising early concerns, James Hamlin finding copied data and thesis plagiarism, PRL expression of concern).
framing_note: Flagship: MYSTERY plus the self-correction drill, and the sub-strand's clearest lesson in extraordinary-claims discipline. T1 keys the hovering magnet -- a thing the kid can watch, not a definition of superconductivity. ACCURACY RAIL (non-negotiable; three separate things that must never be blurred): (a) high-temperature superconductivity is REAL and its mechanism is genuinely unexplained; (b) LK-99 was a claim that FAILED REPLICATION for a mundane reason -- an impurity phase -- and is not established fraud; (c) Dias's two Nature papers were RETRACTED and his university found misconduct. Fourth rail: the hydride superconductors near 200-250 K are real but only under roughly 150-170 GPa of pressure -- never call them room-temperature superconductors without stating the pressure. Dinner-test payoff: T5b (a viral levitation video was settled in about three weeks by strangers who simply made the material themselves). Distractor mine: adjacent-but-wrong real physics -- perfect conductivity confused with the Meissner effect (a superconductor EXPELS magnetic field, it is not merely a resistanceless wire; that deserves its own corrected-misconception rung), phonon-only pairing, the isotope effect -- plus the real names Onnes, Meissner, Abrikosov, Josephson, Bednorz, Muller and Chu. Teach 'critical temperature', 'Meissner effect' and 'retraction' before testing them. VISION: T5c is the bank's stance rung -- a lone critic was dismissed, a top journal published twice, and the co-authors had to force the retraction. Present the RECORD in active voice with the people named; do not editorialise, do not moralise, and do not widen it into a general attack on journals or peer review.

name: Ball lightning: the anomaly in the unexplained drawer
scope: Centuries of credible reports, one spectrum, and no accepted mechanism. T1: on 21 October 1638, during a violent storm, witnesses at St Pancras church in Widecombe-in-the-Moor, Devon reported a ball of fire entering the building during the afternoon service, hovering, splitting in two and exploding -- four people were killed and the roof was wrecked; it is one of the oldest detailed accounts of what is now called ball lightning. T2: the reports are eerily consistent across centuries and continents -- a glowing sphere usually 10 to 30 cm across, drifting horizontally about a metre off the ground at a few metres per second, lasting a handful of seconds, sometimes passing through a closed window, and ending either silently or with a bang, often leaving a sharp smell of ozone. T3: it killed a scientist. On 6 August 1753 in St Petersburg, Georg Wilhelm Richmann was measuring atmospheric electricity with an ungrounded iron rod, following up Franklin's work, when a blue ball of fire reportedly struck him in the head. T4: for three centuries there was no instrument record at all -- until 2012, when a Chinese team on the Qinghai Plateau had two slitless spectrographs trained on ordinary cloud-to-ground lightning from 900 metres away and accidentally caught a ball's spectrum: the emission lines were silicon, iron and calcium -- the elements of SOIL, not of air. T5: that fits the leading chemical hypothesis (John Abrahamson and James Dinniss, Nature, 2000): a strike vaporises silicon out of the ground, which condenses into a fluffy nanoparticle network that glows for seconds while it slowly oxidises in air. It is a hypothesis, not a verdict -- laboratories have produced glowing silicon-oxidation balls lasting several seconds and microwave-cavity plasmoids lasting up to twenty, Pyotr Kapitsa's microwave-resonance idea is still on the table, and no lab has reproduced the full phenomenon. Science has filed ball lightning as REAL and UNEXPLAINED, and left it there.
source: Grokipedia 'Ball lightning' (read via browser -- typical diameters 10-30 cm, median ~35 cm across 5,000+ reports, median duration ~6 s, speeds ~1-10 m/s averaging ~3 m/s, luminosity comparable to a 40 W bulb, colours, penetration of closed windows, ozone/nitrogen-dioxide smell; Gervase of Canterbury's 7 June 1195 account near London; the 21 October 1638 Great Thunderstorm at St Pancras church, Widecombe-in-the-Moor -- fireball entering through a window, splitting, four killed including George Ley; Georg Wilhelm Richmann killed 6 August 1753 in St Petersburg by a blue ball of fire while using an ungrounded rod; R. C. Jennison's 19 March 1963 sighting of a ~20 cm sphere moving down the aisle of an Eastern Airlines aircraft; a 1960s NASA compilation of 112 reports, 87% spherical and 76% uniformly bright; the 2012 Qinghai Plateau video and first natural spectrum, two slitless spectrographs at 900 m, Si I / Fe I / Ca I emission lines matching soil constituents, orb ~5 m across lasting 1.64 s at ~7.6 m/s; effective temperatures ~2000-2700 K; silicon-arc laboratory balls 1-4 cm lasting up to 8 s attributed to slow oxidation of silicon nanoparticles with SiO2 residue confirmed; microwave-cavity plasmoids at 2.45 GHz lasting up to 20 s; explicit statement that no unified theory is established). BUILD NOTE: the Abrahamson and Dinniss Nature 2000 citation should be re-verified directly before a rung names the paper.
framing_note: MYSTERY told as honest anomaly handling -- the strand's model for how science treats a phenomenon it cannot explain but will not dismiss. T1 keys the SCENE (a fireball in a church during service, 1638) and must be phrased as a REPORT, not narrated as verified physics: seventeenth-century testimony is evidence, not measurement. ACCURACY RAIL: ball lightning is now accepted as a real phenomenon with an UNKNOWN mechanism -- do not present it as debunked, and do not let the 2012 Qinghai spectrum be written as proof of the Abrahamson-Dinniss mechanism; it is evidence that the glowing material came from soil. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (they were pointing their instruments at ordinary lightning and caught the ghost by accident). MYSTERY DISCIPLINE: no distractor may secretly be the true mechanism -- rungs must ask what the 2012 spectrum SHOWED or what a NAMED hypothesis PROPOSES. Distractor mine: real adjacent phenomena people genuinely confuse it with, each with a known explanation -- St Elmo's fire (a corona glow that stays attached to a mast or wingtip), sprites and blue jets (real upper-atmosphere discharges), lens flare and retinal afterimages from a nearby strike, and will-o'-the-wisp marsh gas. Using those as distractors quietly teaches four real things. Teach 'emission line' and 'spectrograph' before testing them.
history_overlap: history bank -- the Great Thunderstorm of Widecombe-in-the-Moor as a 1638 English parish episode with named victims; the science rung must key the PHENOMENON and its 2012 spectrum, not the village's story.

name: Why ice is slippery
scope: The everyday mystery hiding under your boots -- and the textbook answer that is wrong. T1: almost every textbook says a skater's blade presses down so hard it melts a thin lubricating film of water -- and that explanation fails: the pressure a skater actually exerts lowers ice's melting point by only a fraction of a degree, yet ice stays slippery at minus 20 C and colder, where no plausible pressure would melt it. T2: the pressure idea is not crankery -- James Thomson proposed it in 1849 and his brother William, Lord Kelvin, confirmed that pressure genuinely does lower ice's melting point, and John Joly extended it in 1886. The physics is real; the SIZE of the effect is far too small to do the job. T3: Michael Faraday's rival idea from 1842 -- the surface of ice is already disordered and liquid-like even when the block beneath is frozen solid; that is why two ice cubes pressed together fuse into one (regelation) and why a snowball packs but dry sand does not. T4: Frank Bowden and T. P. Hughes' 1939 answer -- the sliding ITSELF heats the contact and melts a micro-layer -- which explains a moving skate beautifully and does not explain why ice is slippery when you are standing perfectly still. T5: measurement settled the existence of the quasi-liquid layer without settling the argument -- it is real, a few nanometres thick near minus 10 C and thickening towards micrometres near 0 C, and recent work argues its molecules are weakly bound and can roll rather than truly flow; figure skaters get their best combination of grip and glide near minus 5.5 C, which is itself evidence against pure pressure-melting. Which mechanism dominates in which regime is still openly debated.
source: Wikipedia 'Ice' slipperiness section (pressure-melting fails because skaters would experience far more friction than they do, and because figure skating works best at -5.5 C while pressure-melting predicts skating below -4 C would be impossible; Bowden and Hughes 1939 frictional melting and its failure to explain slipperiness at rest; surface premelting -- interface molecules cannot bond properly with the bulk and remain semi-liquid; recent atomic-force-microscopy work finding a high coefficient of friction that complicates premelting; the article states the mechanism controlling ice friction 'is still an active area of scientific study', with a 2014 study suggesting frictional heating dominates under most typical conditions); Wikipedia 'Premelting' (Faraday's 1842 observation that two blocks of ice freeze together, with his snowball/moist-sand comparison; Tammann 1910 and Stranski 1942 on surface-initiated melting; Frenkel on the absence of superheating in solids; quasi-liquid layer nanometres thick near -10 C and micrometres nearer the melting point; the three competing mechanisms named -- pressure melting from James Thomson 1849 and John Joly 1886, premelting from Faraday and Tyndall, frictional heating from Bowden; modern consensus rejects pressure melting as dominant since ice stays slippery below -20 C, while premelting versus frictional heating remains debated). BUILD NOTE: Grokipedia not yet read -- run Grokipedia-first on 'Ice' and 'Premelting' before authoring.
framing_note: MYSTERY hiding in plain sight, and the sub-strand's best TEST-IT-YOURSELF topic. T1 is a corrected-misconception rung and the dinner-test payoff -- the answer in the schoolbook is wrong, and the kid can say so at the table tonight. ACCURACY RAIL: pressure-melting is real physics that is simply TOO SMALL to explain the effect -- never write it as fake or invented; the honest sentence is 'the effect exists and is nowhere near big enough'. Second rail: say plainly that the question is OPEN -- premelting versus frictional heating is still argued -- so no distractor may secretly be the true mechanism; rungs must ask which mechanism a NAMED scientist proposed or what a NAMED measurement found. INVITATION: this is checkable at home and should be framed that way -- a thin wire with weights on each end will slowly cut through an ice block and leave it in one piece (regelation), and a cube slides differently on freezer-cold ice than on ice near melting. Distractor mine: the four historically live answers themselves (pressure melting, frictional heating, premelting, a trapped air film) plus the real names Thomson, Kelvin, Joly, Faraday, Tyndall and Bowden -- all respectable, each wrong in a different way. LANE: glacier basal sliding at a named glacier is geography.
history_overlap: geography bank -- glacier movement, basal sliding and regelation at named glaciers are place-anchored earth processes there; science keeps the surface physics, the failed pressure explanation and the skating-rink test.

name: The antimatter ledger: why is there anything at all?
scope: The deepest open account in physics, and it balances to almost nothing. T1: bring a particle together with its antiparticle and both vanish completely into light -- no ash, no fragments, one hundred per cent of the mass converted to energy; it is the only reaction in nature that spends matter entirely. T2: it was PREDICTED before it was seen. Paul Dirac's 1928 equation carried a second solution he could not delete, implying a positively charged twin of the electron; in 1932 Carl Anderson photographed exactly that -- a cosmic-ray track in a cloud chamber curving the wrong way in a magnetic field. T3: the ledger problem, and the reason you exist -- the Big Bang should have produced matter and antimatter in equal amounts, which would have annihilated into nothing but light; instead roughly one particle in a billion survived, and every atom you have ever touched is made of that leftover. T4: Andrei Sakharov set the terms in 1967 with three conditions any successful explanation must meet -- baryon number must be violated, C and CP symmetry must both be violated, and the reactions must happen out of thermal equilibrium. T4b: CP violation is not speculation, it was MEASURED -- James Cronin and Val Fitch found neutral kaons decaying in a way that treats matter and antimatter differently in 1964 and took the 1980 Nobel Prize, and the BaBar and Belle experiments measured more of it in B mesons from 2001. T5: and it is nowhere near enough -- the CP violation the Standard Model permits is orders of magnitude too small to leave one survivor per billion, so the asymmetry is honestly unexplained; leptogenesis and neutrino CP violation (the T2K hints) are candidates, not answers. T5b: physicists keep hunting for any difference at all: CERN's ALPHA experiment traps antihydrogen atoms in a magnetic bottle, and in September 2023 ALPHA-g reported that antihydrogen FALLS DOWN like ordinary matter, closing off the antigravity escape route, while antihydrogen's light spectrum matches hydrogen's to extraordinary precision. Every test so far says antimatter is a perfect mirror -- which makes the survival of matter harder to explain, not easier.
source: Wikipedia 'Baryon asymmetry' (the asymmetry parameter eta -- roughly one extra baryon per billion photons, with ~411 CMB photons per cubic centimetre at 2.725 K; Sakharov's three 1967 conditions stated in full -- baryon number violation, C and CP violation, out-of-equilibrium interactions; Cronin and Fitch 1964 'Evidence for the 2-pi decay of the K0-2 meson' with neutral kaons, Nobel Prize 1980; the explicit statement that Standard Model CP violation is insufficient to account for the observed asymmetry; B-meson CP violation around 2001; T2K neutrino hints and leptogenesis; described as one of the great mysteries in physics with no consensus theory); Wikipedia 'ALPHA experiment' (magnetic minimum-B trap using a superconducting octupole and solenoid mirror coils, holding atoms below one kelvin; laser cooling of antihydrogen; antihydrogen-versus-hydrogen spectroscopy as a CPT test; the 27 September 2023 ALPHA-g publication finding antimatter interacts with gravity similarly to ordinary matter and ruling out repulsive antigravity); Wikipedia 'List of unsolved problems in physics' (baryon asymmetry entry). BUILD NOTE: Grokipedia not yet read -- run Grokipedia-first on 'Baryon asymmetry', 'Antimatter' and 'CP violation'; also verify Anderson's 1932 positron discovery details directly before the T2 rung names the cloud chamber.
framing_note: MYSTERY at the largest possible scale, and the sub-strand's grandest ladder. T1 keys the vivid physical fact (total annihilation into light), not a definition of antimatter. ACCURACY RAIL (the one that trips people): CP violation IS real, IS measured and IS in the Standard Model -- the honest statement is that it is far too SMALL to account for the observed asymmetry, never that it is absent or hypothetical. Second rail: Anderson found the positron in COSMIC RAYS in a cloud chamber in 1932, not in an accelerator; and Dirac PREDICTED it from an equation, which is the whole wonder of T2. Third rail: leptogenesis and neutrino CP violation are live CANDIDATES, not the answer -- T5 must say plainly that no one yet knows why anything survived. Dinner-test payoff: T3 (you are made entirely of the one-in-a-billion leftover). MYSTERY DISCIPLINE: no distractor may secretly be the truth -- mechanism rungs must ask what Sakharov REQUIRED or what Cronin and Fitch MEASURED. Distractor mine: real adjacent physics that is correct but answers a different question -- the Dirac sea, dark matter, dark energy, neutrino oscillation -- plus the genuinely searched-for-and-not-found idea of distant antimatter galaxies or domains, and the real names Dirac, Anderson, Sakharov, Cronin and Fitch. Teach 'antiparticle', 'annihilation' and 'CP symmetry' in plain language before any rung tests them; keep the whole ladder inside the grade-10 ceiling -- no field theory, no Lagrangians, no gauge language. LANE: philosophy owns the metaphysical version of this question.
history_overlap: philosophy bank -- Leibniz's 'why is there something rather than nothing' and cosmological arguments are philosophy's ground; the science rungs must key the measured one-in-a-billion ledger, Sakharov's three conditions, the kaon result and the CERN antihydrogen tests, never the metaphysics.

name: Heard once, never again: the Wow! signal and the perytons
scope: How astronomers log a mystery, rank the hypotheses, and refuse to hand down a verdict. T1: on 15 August 1977 the Ohio State 'Big Ear' radio telescope printed out a narrow radio signal so far above the background noise that when Jerry Ehman read the paper days later he circled it in red pen and wrote a single word beside it -- 'Wow!' -- which is now the signal's name. T2: what he circled, '6EQUJ5', is not a code and not a message: it is the signal's INTENSITY written as one character per 12 seconds as it rose and fell, and the U marks a peak about thirty times the noise level. T3: the signal lasted exactly 72 seconds, which is precisely how long a fixed point in the sky takes to drift through Big Ear's beam -- so it behaved like something out there in space rather than interference down here on the ground; and it sat near 1420 MHz, the hydrogen line, the very frequency SETI researchers had argued a careful broadcaster would choose. T4: it has never repeated. Roughly fifty follow-up searches, including with the Very Large Array, have found nothing -- and hypotheses get RANKED, not crowned: Antonio Paris' 2017 proposal that hydrogen clouds around comets 266P/Christensen and 335P/Gibbs made the signal was rejected on the evidence (wrong position, wrong beam, comets do not emit strongly there), and a 2024 proposal has a stellar flare briefly lighting a cold hydrogen cloud into a natural maser. T4b: the discipline in miniature, and the best story in the strand -- in 2007 Duncan Lorimer and his student David Narkevic found a five-millisecond radio blast buried in 2001 archive data from the Parkes telescope, and Parkes went on to record sixteen more similar signals nicknamed 'perytons'; in 2015 a team led by Emily Petroff traced the perytons to the observatory's own MICROWAVE OVENS, whose magnetrons emitted a burst whenever a staff member yanked the door open mid-cycle. Check your own kitchen before you announce the universe. T5: and the real ones survived the check -- fast radio bursts turned out to be genuine and extragalactic; FRB 121102 repeated and was pinned to a dwarf galaxy about three billion light-years away, and in April 2020 FRB 200428 was traced to a magnetar inside our own galaxy, SGR 1935+2154, proving magnetars can make them. That explains one source, not the whole population -- and the Wow! signal still has no accepted explanation at all.
source: Wikipedia 'Wow! signal' (15 August 1977 at 22:16 EST, Big Ear at Ohio State near Delaware, Ohio; Jerry R. Ehman circling '6EQUJ5' and writing 'Wow!'; the string as intensity-over-time with U about thirty standard deviations above background; duration exactly 72 seconds, matching the telescope's observation window; 1420.4556 MHz, about 50 kHz above the hydrogen line, bandwidth under 10 kHz; rise-and-fall profile consistent with a celestial source; never recurred across about fifty search attempts including Big Ear and the VLA; Antonio Paris' 2017 comet hypothesis for 266P/Christensen and 335P/Gibbs and the specific grounds for its rejection; the 2024 Planetary Habitability Laboratory maser-flare proposal; source remains unconfirmed); Wikipedia 'Fast radio burst' (Lorimer and Narkevic 2007 discovery in Parkes archive data recorded 24 July 2001, FRB 010724, under 5 ms and 30 Jy; 16 perytons detected at Parkes from 2010, resolved in 2015 to microwave oven doors opened during a heating cycle with emission from the magnetron during power-down; FRB 121102 found November 2012 with Arecibo, ten repeat bursts identified by Paul Scholz in November 2015, localised in 2017 to a dwarf galaxy about three billion light-years away with an extreme rotation measure; FRB 200428 in April 2020 from the Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154 at about 30,000 light-years, establishing magnetars as one source while the mechanism remains unknown; the full population still unexplained). BUILD NOTE: Grokipedia not yet read -- run Grokipedia-first on 'Wow! signal' and 'Fast radio burst'; verify Emily Petroff's lead authorship on the 2015 peryton paper directly before the T4b rung names her.
framing_note: CONCEPT/THEME ladder on how astronomers handle one-off signals: log it, rank the hypotheses, withhold the verdict, and suspect yourself first. ACCURACY RAIL (two, both load-bearing): the Wow! signal is UNEXPLAINED -- it is neither evidence of aliens nor debunked -- and no rung may imply anything was decoded, because 6EQUJ5 is an intensity trace and carries no content whatsoever; and magnetars are a CONFIRMED source of at least one fast radio burst, not the confirmed explanation of all of them. Dinner-test payoff: T4b -- a world-class observatory chased a cosmic mystery for five years and it was the staff microwave. That rung is the purest expression of Feynman's first principle in the whole sub-strand: you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool (that quote IS documented -- 'Cargo Cult Science', adapted from his 1974 Caltech commencement address). INVITATION: T1 and T3 support a night-sky framing -- the hydrogen line is why radio astronomers watch that frequency, and the 72 seconds is just the sky turning. MYSTERY DISCIPLINE: no distractor may secretly be the truth on the Wow! rungs. Distractor mine: real radio anomalies that DO have answers, which teaches four extra things while distracting -- pulsars (Jocelyn Bell Burnell's 1967 signal briefly labelled LGM-1 and then shown to be a spinning neutron star), the perytons themselves, satellite and radar interference, and quasars. Teach 'dispersion measure' and 'magnetar' in plain words before testing them. Build note: Bell Burnell's LGM-1 may belong to a sibling discovery sub-strand -- use it as a DISTRACTOR here rather than building a rung on it.
